## Ruling recorded — option A: no copy affordance on masked field types (director seat, decision batch #83, 2026-09-08)

Maintainer's reply, verbatim (live PM chat, 2026-09-08T03:4xZ, answering the batch #83 presentation where this card was item 3 with recommendation A):

> 其他同意

⇒ In `DetailSection`, rows whose field type the `fields` package masks (`password`, `secret`) are not copy-interactive: no row click, no Enter/Space, no hover copy button reaches `handleCopyField`. The per-type refusal the cell renderer applies is honoured by the copy handler. ⛔ Not B — copying `••••••` is a second silent wrong answer.

Pin: a rendered `DetailSection` with a `password` row asserts nothing reaches `navigator.clipboard.writeText`; a control asserts an ordinary text row still copies its own value. ⛔ Independent of objectui#8395 (object-valued cells) — different branch of the handler.

Label: `needs-user-decision` → `pm:queue`. ⛔ Not dispatched by this seat.

## ⭐ The direction is RULED. Implement A; do not re-open it.

Maintainer ruling, director seat, decision batch #83, 2026-09-08 (comment 5578821128): **A — no copy affordance on masked field types.** Rows whose field type the `fields` package masks (`password`, `secret`) are not copy-interactive.

⛔ **Not B.** Copying `••••••` was considered and refused — it is a second silent wrong answer.

I am naming this because the failure mode I hit twice today is *writing a fence against a decision that had already been made*. This one is made. Nothing in your measurement reopens it; if your measurement contradicts the ruling's premise, **report and stop**, do not choose.

## ⚠️ The card's reading is STALE — the file has moved under it

The card reads `packages/plugin-detail/src/DetailSection.tsx` at `ca3942729af817b3e017b8dcb99e1a4826a603f9` and quotes line 220:

```ts
const textValue = value !== null && value !== undefined ? String(value) : '';
```

**objectui#8395 closed on 2026-09-08 and its PR #8460 merged — and it changed `handleCopyField` itself** (object-valued cells now copy as JSON rather than `[object Object]`). ⇒ the line the card quotes may no longer exist in that form, and the handler's shape is different from what this card describes.

Re-read `handleCopyField`, `copyInteractive`, `canCopy` and `canInlineEditField` **on your own base**, and report what you found. ⚠️ Line 220, the `String(value)` spelling, and the two `fields/src/index.tsx` mask registrations at ~2380 are all snapshot facts.

## ⭐ Three reach paths, not one — this is the discriminating axis

The card measured the affordance reaching `handleCopyField` by **three** routes, and the ruling names all three:

1. the **row click**,
2. **Enter / Space** on the row,
3. the **hover copy button**.

`copyInteractive = canCopy && !canInlineEditField`; `canCopy` is `hasCellValue(value)` (true for any non-empty string) and `canInlineEditField` is false because `password` / `secret` sit in `isInlineExcludedDetailFieldType` — objectui#4221 put them there precisely because the row has no real value to seed an editor with. ⇒ the exclusion that protects the *write* direction is exactly what leaves the *read* direction exposed.

⚠️ **A fix that removes only the button leaves two live paths and will pass a careless pin.** Pin all three.

## ⚠️ The pin is absence-shaped, which is the shape that passes by never running

The ruling's pin is *"a rendered `DetailSection` with a `password` row asserts nothing reaches `navigator.clipboard.writeText`"*. **An assertion never observed to fail has not been tested** — and a "was not called" assertion passes when the row never rendered, when the click never landed, when the component threw during mount, and when the spy was installed on the wrong object.

So it is only evidence if, in the same file:

- the **control row** (ordinary text) fires `writeText` with its own value **through the same interaction shape** — i.e. the spy is proved able to reach 1, and the interaction is proved able to reach the handler;
- the masked row is proved to have **rendered** (assert the mask `••••••` is on screen) before asserting the absence;
- each of the three paths is exercised on **both** rows, so a path that silently does nothing on *every* row cannot read as a fix.

⚠️ happy-dom notes that bit this file's neighbours: `window.innerWidth` had to be pinned to 1280 for the card's own measurement, and `queryByText` throws on **multiple** matches as well as none. Count at the spy, not with a text query.

## ⭐ Non-regression: derive it from what a plausible WRONG FIX would still satisfy

The wrong fix that satisfies every vivid assertion is **gating on `canCopy` / `hasCellValue`**. It makes the password row non-copy-interactive — and it also changes **which rows count as empty**, because `hasCellValue` is objectui#8376's *emptiness authority* for this component, not a copy predicate. ⇒ your load-bearing pins are:

1. **the emptiness classification of every row type is unchanged**, and
2. **ordinary rows — including the object-valued ones PR #8460 just fixed — still copy exactly what they copy today.** ⚠️ Re-read #8460's pins; your change must leave them green, and if it cannot, that is a finding, not a licence.

State the caricature as *the mutation that makes the code answer the same thing for everything* — here **"nothing is ever copy-interactive."** It must redden the control loudly.

## ⚠️ One design question I am NOT ruling — measure it and report

The masked set today is two names (`password`, `secret`, registered in `packages/fields/src/index.tsx`). **Hardcoding that pair in `plugin-detail` mints a second authority for "which types are masked"** — the AGENTS.md #0.1 shape — and it silently fails to protect a third masked type the day one is added.

⇒ **Look for an existing way to ask the `fields` registry whether a type is masked.** If one exists, use it. If none does, ⛔ **do not invent one in `plugin-detail`** — report what you found, ship the narrowest correct thing the ruling permits, and file the "the mask has no queryable authority" finding as its own card. Say explicitly which of the two you did.

## Verification standard

- **Verify by CONTENT, never by exit code or sha.** Assert on what reaches `navigator.clipboard.writeText`.
- Ask of every pin: **"Would an implementation strictly worse than the bug pass this?"**
- **Ablation:** mutate a READ SITE (never the pin), from a committed tree, `trap` on EXIT/INT/TERM with absolute paths. Prove the mutation landed **on disk in both directions** (anchor counts before/after AND `git hash-object` vs the HEAD blob) **plus a line-total gate**. Restore **by state** (`git diff HEAD` empty). **A void leg is VOID, not green; a leg that lands but does not discriminate is NEGATIVE, not void — report it as negative.**
- **LEG D: classify per-test from vitest's JSON reporter** (`--reporter=json --outputFile`), ⛔ never the text reporter. Count death strings separately (`Element type is invalid`, `Failed Suites`, `No test suite found in file`, `Tests  no tests`, `Transform failed`).
- Run vitest **from the repo root with paths** — `pnpm --filter PKG exec vitest run FILE` is refused by guard objectui#3378 and `cd packages/X && pnpm exec vitest` silently re-roots onto `apps/console`. ⛔ `--no-inline-config` is an objectstack convention and manufactures errors here CI does not have.
- `search_issues` returns **false zeros** on this repo — declare the channel, never claim a dedup you could not perform. `skip-changeset` is a **phantom label**; the real exemption is an **empty-frontmatter** changeset.

## Contract review — accepted. PR #8685 is out of draft and armed.

## ⚠️ First, my dispatch was wrong about the most important number

I wrote *"⭐ Three reach paths, not one — the discriminating axis"* and told you to pin all three. **There are five.**

> `DetailSection` also renders a **mobile grouped-inset row** whose click and Enter/Space are gated on `canCopy` **alone**, and the **desktop hover button was gated on `canCopy` too** rather than on `copyInteractive`.

I inherited the count from the card and stated it as the axis the fix turns on. A dev who trusted my "three" would have shipped a fix that **left two live paths handing the credential to the clipboard** — and every pin I specified would have been green. The card measured three; nobody had measured the mobile branch.

⇒ that is the second time today a dispatch of mine carried a card's number as if it were a reading. The instruction that saved it is the generic one — *re-locate by content on your own base and report what you found* — not any specific warning I wrote.

## ⭐ The gate derivation, and the sentence that shows the non-regression axis was understood rather than obeyed

```
canCopy       (unchanged — the shared emptiness reader, hasCellValue)
copyOffered   = canCopy && !isMaskedField
copyInteractive = copyOffered && !canInlineEditField
```

All five paths withdrawn through **one** derived gate rather than five edits. And then this:

> The refusal is deliberately **NOT** spelled into `canCopy`: that name is a reader of the shared emptiness authority `hasCellValue`, and **a masked row is not an empty one.**

That is exactly the wrong fix my dispatch named — *"gating on `canCopy` / `hasCellValue`… because `hasCellValue` is objectui#8376's emptiness authority, not a copy predicate"* — declined **with the reason restated in the dev's own terms**, which is the difference between avoiding a trap and understanding it. LEG E proves it: making masked rows count as EMPTY reddens **17 pins including the emptiness non-regression pin**.

⭐ And `isMaskedDetailFieldType` answers the **narrow-only union** of the authored view type and the object-schema type, matching the two gates beside it (objectui#3355) — *"so a presentation override can withdraw the affordance but never restore it on a credential column."* On a credential boundary that is the correct direction for tolerance to run, and it was chosen rather than inherited.

## ⭐ LEG C and LEG D are the legs this card needed

- **LEG C** — the desktop hover button alone reverted to `canCopy` → **4 red, exactly the button pins.**
- **LEG D** — the mobile block alone reverted to `canCopy` → **6 red, exactly the mobile pins.**

⇒ a **button-only** fix is caught, and a **desktop-only** fix is caught. For a defect whose whole shape is *"several paths reach the same handler and a careless fix closes one"*, those two legs are the review; the caricature (LEG B, 21 red) proves much less by comparison. And every leg's failure set is *exactly* its own family — no leg reddens a neighbour, so the pins are proved independent rather than assumed to be.

The absence-shaped pin is also built the way it had to be: all five paths exercised on **both** the masked rows **and an ordinary control row in the same mounted tree**; the mask proved rendered and the raw value proved **absent from the document** before any absence is asserted; and absence counted at `writeText.mock.calls` rather than with a text query — necessary here, since **both masked rows draw identical bullets** and `queryByText` throws on multiple matches.

## ⭐ The fenced design question: mirrored, and said so

I fenced this: *look for an existing way to ask the registry whether a type is masked; if none exists, ⛔ do not invent one — report, ship the narrowest thing, file the finding. **Say explicitly which of the two you did.***

> **I MIRRORED, I DID NOT INVENT AN AUTHORITY.** No queryable "is type T masked" exists in `@object-ui/fields` (searched `isMasked` / `MASKED_FIELD` / `maskedType` / `isCredential` / `CREDENTIAL_FIELD` across packages and apps: **zero hits, with a control grep proving the path filter works**); the mask is two anonymous renderers inside `getCellRenderer`'s standard map.

Zero hits **with a control proving the filter works** — because `git grep -- 'packages/*/src'` matches nothing at all in this repo, and a broken path filter is indistinguishable from a real absence. The mirror is documented **in place as a mirror, not an authority**, with **both** of its costs declared: a third masked type would not reach it, and `registerFieldRenderer` can replace the mask at runtime, which no static set can see. Filed as objectui#8686.

⇒ that is the honest shape. The card is fixed, the duplicate authority is **named as a duplicate at its own site** rather than quietly becoming the second source of truth, and the real question is on the record instead of being settled by whoever happened to need it first.

## The card's own readings, corrected

Both stale, both reported, and neither load-bearing — the right way round:

- the quoted line 220 `String(value)` is **gone** (the handler is the post-#8395 shape), and the mask registrations are at `fields/src/index.tsx:**2465-2466**`, not 2380-2381;
- but every premise **held**: `canCopy` is still `hasCellValue(value)`, `canInlineEditField` is still false for `password`/`secret` via `isInlineExcludedDetailFieldType`, so `copyInteractive` was still true on a credential row.

Non-regression confirmed where it counts: **the object-valued rows PR #8460 just fixed copy byte-for-byte what they copied before**, and #8395 / #8376 / #8474's pins are untouched and green across 149 files.

## On your open question

**A** is my reading too — converge the read direction onto the shape the write direction already has (`isInlineExcludedFieldType`) and delete the mirror. ⛔ But I am not ruling it here, and objectui#8686 is the right place: **C** (a `@objectstack/spec` credential fact, with the renderer's mask a *consequence* rather than the source) is a contract question, and this session has learned twice this week what happens when a consumer-side seat settles one of those. Nothing blocks on it — the PR ships the narrowest thing the ruling permits.
